native_source_locators.text: > Inspect local Zarr metadata rather than requiring a filename substring. Validate Zarr node kind/format independently from `attributes.ome.version`; distinguish a supported OME-Zarr 0.5 image/organization, another version, a generic Zarr group and malformed metadata. For a selected image group, use its multiscales metadata. For a plate, follow `plate.wells[].path` and each well's `well.images[].path`. For a transitional `bioformats2raw.layout` collection, give plate metadata precedence; otherwise read `attributes.ome.series` from `OME/zarr.json`, resolving its image-group paths in the collection's root namespace. If that layout has no series or plate metadata, use its consecutively numbered image groups beginning at 0. For other local hierarchies, discover candidate image groups by bounded, cancellable metadata traversal and validate their OME image metadata; do not apply the numbered-collection convention to arbitrary Zarr groups or treat every array as an image. List all discovered source images with stable group paths, retaining usable siblings when one image fails. Resolve every `datasets[].path` relative to its image group in metadata order; never construct a level path from an integer index. Keep associated labels as overlays for their source images. Preserve a supplied image-group subpath rather than replacing it with the enclosing `.zarr` root.

native_source_locators.text: Viewer.md:5 opens a chosen fileset; it does not own general folder indexing, persistent CSV/catalogs or a local HTTP service. Proposal: optional user-initiated parent-folder discovery with cheap cancellable thumbnails and a per-fileset link to the complete metadata-derived image list. Benefit: find large collections; dependencies: traversal limits, partial-error reporting, stable identities and an explicitly located cache outside source data; tradeoffs: scan/I/O cost, stale indexes and more navigation UI. Indexing must not stop permanently at an unrecognized wrapper or hide sparse/nonnumeric fields behind a successful thumbnail. Acceptance after approval: wrappers, extensionless roots, sparse fields, arbitrary series, unreadable directories, cancellation and unchanged source trees. native_source_locators.text: **Saved-display proposal requiring approval.** Recommend using valid saved `omero.channels` label/color/active/start/end and valid rdefs defaultT/defaultZ/model as initial session settings, with user changes retained for that session. The real [6001240 image metadata](https://livingobjects.ebi.ac.uk/idr/zarr/v0.5/idr0062A/6001240_labels.zarr/zarr.json) (S00011) has LaminB1 blue and Dapi yellow, windows 0–1500 while min/max are 0–65535, and defaultZ=118. Benefit: recognizable opening display and no mandatory level-0 extrema scan. Dependencies: channel/axis validation and renderer transfer functions. Tradeoffs: saved settings can be stale or malformed, and dtype-wide fallback can look low contrast. Proposed fallback: validate each field independently, use deterministic session defaults for absent/invalid settings, bound indices, and identify fallback use. A sampled-statistics alternative may improve contrast but costs I/O and must be labeled sampled, never global extrema. Exact fallback palette/window and whether to use saved active flags require review; the spec describes optional producer metadata rather than mandating a particular viewer UI. Acceptance after approval: the specimen uses end=1500, not max=65535, and plane 118 when available; absent/invalid omero remains viewable with explained fallback; no full-resolution scan blocks opening; changes never rewrite the store.
